newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1996 TV imports exceed domestic output.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1996 TV imports exceed domestic output.

text.p: Japan's imports of television sets rose to a record 7.51 million in calendar 1996, exceeding domestic TV output for the first time, the Electronic Industries Association of Japan (EIAJ) said on Tuesday.
Imports of videocassette recorders (VCRs) rose 46.9 percent in 1996 from a year earlier to a record 4.60 million units, the EIAJ said in a statement.
On a volume basis, Japan's TV imports rose 0.7 percent last year from the previous year, while its domestic production of TVs fell a year-on-year 17.5 percent to 6.48 million units, the EIAJ said.
"Japan's TV imports (in 1996) slightly exceeded their 1995 level and were the highest on record," the EIAJ said.
"Partly due to a fall in domestic production, imports surpassed domestic output for the first time ever on an annual basis," it added.

In 1996, Malaysia topped the list of exporters of TVs to Japan at 2.41 million units, up a year-on-year 2.2 percent, followed by Thailand which exported 1.59 million units, up a year-on-year 5.1 percent, the EIAJ said.
China, the third largest TV exporter to Japan in 1996, exported 1.09 million units, marking a steep 29.7 percent rise from a year ago, the EIAJ said.

The industry association said that the trend of surging imports had come to a halt. "Due to the yen's fall and the completion of Japanese makers' shift of their production bases to other countries, we believe that the dramatic increase in imports has completely stopped."

Japanese electronics companies have built plants in Asian countries such as Malaysia and Thailand due to the impact of the strong yen in recent years, industry analysts said. A strong yen weakens the price competitiveness of Japan's domestically produced goods in overseas markets, they said.

Japan's VCR imports may exceed domestic production in the future if current trends continue, the EIAJ said, although it added that on a monthly basis VCR imports fell in December for the first time in 44 months.
Japan's domestic VCR output in 1996 was down 21.1 percent year-on-year to 9.98 million units due to increased imports, the EIAJ said.
The association said Japan's exports of TVs and VCRs in 1996 fell to their lowest level since 1988.
Japan's 1996 TV exports were down 18.9 percent to 2.34 million units and its VCR exports fell 30.6 percent to 6.78 million units, it said.
The EIAJ said Japan's domestic TV shipments, excluding shipments of high-definition TVs, were up 5.5 percent year-on-year to a record 10.11 million units.
Domestic shipments of high-definition TVs rose 132.5 percent to 188,000 units, the EIAJ said.
Japan's domestic shipments of VCRs rose 10.4 percent year-on-year to 6.67 million units, it said.
